title: Map and mitigate OpenAI Responses compatibility gaps affecting streaming, function-calling, and structured outputs
creator: Ava Chen
description: This ticket captures a targeted compatibility mapping and mitigation plan between Redwood's Responses-compatible API surface and the OpenAI Responses API. The goal is to identify concrete parity gaps across three priority areas (streaming semantics, function/tool calling, and structured outputs), produce an adapter design that preserves Redwood runtime performance guarantees, and land a backwards-compatible opt-in compatibility flag for partner customers and migrations. This work is scoped to: 1) document observable behavioral differences and failure cases, 2) propose minimally-invasive adapter transformations, 3) implement translation logic + tests, and 4) run staged canaries with real traffic. The outcome should be a documented compatibility layer and a risk/rollback playbook.
technical_findings: Streaming format mismatch: OpenAI uses incremental 'delta' objects with nested role/content tokens while Redwood's streaming path emits per-token fragments optimized for lower latency; naive passthrough breaks tool-call completion detection and client-side reconstruction.

Function/tool-calling differences: OAI semantics expect a single JSON string return in some cases and use 'finish_reason' values that do not always map cleanly to Redwood's internal call lifecycle (e.g., 'function_call' vs partial function call streaming).

Structured output schema variance: OpenAI examples include 'output_parsed' or 'tool_outputs' shape conventions; Redwood stores structured outputs as typed envelopes. Key mismatches are field names, nesting levels, and optional metadata propagation (e.g., provenance/request_id headers).

Error and fallback behavior: OAI sometimes emits terminal errors mid-stream or uses final 'error' objects; Redwood's runtime prioritizes graceful degradation with automatic fallback to model variants — mapping these semantics needs explicit shim behavior and documented client-visible signals.

Model variant and parameter mapping: Certain OAI model options (e.g., 'response_format' hints, tool-scoping metadata) don't have 1:1 counterpart in our runtime configuration; we must canonicalize options and surface warnings where approximations occur.

Tokenization and chunking: Token-level offsets and token_count fields differ across encoders; some customers rely on these for cost accounting and highlight synchronization — adapter must avoid shifting offsets unexpectedly.

Backpressure and flow-control: Redwood's batching and KV-cache optimizations mean streaming times are bursty; some OAI clients expect consistent per-token pacing — we need to document this and optionally simulate OAI pacing for compatibility clients.
Security/metadata propagation: OAI includes top-level request/response metadata fields that customers use for auditing; adapter must forward or replicate these into our audit logs and trace headers.
proposed_mitigation_options: Adapter layer option A (byte-for-byte emulation): implement a translation layer that converts our token-stream events into OAI-style 'delta' objects, reconstructs function call JSON payloads, and maps finish_reason values. This preserves client expectations at cost of modest CPU + latency overhead.

Adapter layer option B (schema-canonicalization): normalize structured outputs to a canonical envelope at the platform ingress, then emit both native Redwood payloads and an OAI-compatible alias when the compatibility flag is set. Lower runtime overhead for native users, but more complex ingress logic.

Opt-in compatibility flag: expose a request-level/route-level flag 'responses_compat=v1' that activates translation. Default remains native Redwood semantics to avoid regressions for existing customers.

Streaming buffering policy: implement a small bounded buffer that waits for function-call boundary tokens before emitting OAI-style terminal events; buffer size is tunable per route to balance latency vs correctness.
Client SDK shims: provide lightweight SDK helpers (JS/Python) that reassemble our native streams into OAI-style objects for clients that cannot opt-in server-side.
Automated parity tests: add end-to-end scenarios in the evaluation harness covering partial tool-call streams, nested structured outputs, and mid-stream errors with expected OAI-compatible events.
Experimental canary: route a small percentage of traffic (1-2%) through the adapter to measure latency tail impact and incompatibility regressions before wider rollout.
Docs & migration guide: publish a mapping table of fields, known approximations, and a 'gotchas' section for developers migrating from OpenAI Responses to Redwood or vice versa.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility flag 'responses_compat=v1' exists and is documented in the API reference.
Adapter passes the 12 canonical parity unit tests (see test plan) including function-call streaming reconstruction and structured-output field mapping.
No P0 customer-facing regressions observed during 7-day canary at 1% traffic and latency p95 < baseline + 50ms for those routes.
SDK shim published for JS and Python with example migration snippets.
Playbook details for rollback, tracing, and postmortem steps are added to the incident runbook.
Open-source or internal mapping doc published: /docs/responses-compat/mapping-v1 (link in comments).
qa_plan: Unit tests: adapter translation functions (token -> delta, delta -> function-payload) with fuzzed inputs.
Integration tests: full-model end-to-end tests using canary models that exercise streaming+tool calling concurrently.
Compatibility harness: replay recorded OAI Responses sessions (anonymized) and compare reconstructed outputs to golden OAI traces.
Performance benchmarks: measure p50/p95/p99 across canary routes with and without adapter on representative workloads.
Chaos testing: simulate mid-stream model aborts, truncated function outputs, and delayed KV cache hits to ensure adapter signals are robust.
Security review: ensure adapter does not leak internal headers or PII in OAI fields (manual review + automated linter).
rollout_plan: Dev rollout: land feature flag behind 'responses_compat' with unit/integration tests in CI.
Internal alpha: enable for Redwood infra and SDK teams only, collect feedback for 2 weeks.
Canary: enable for 1% of external traffic for 7 days, monitor errors, latency, and replay mismatches.
Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% on compatible routes, with health checks and automated rollback triggers on error spikes.
GA: publish docs, SDK samples, and migration guide; announce to customers and provide a migration window.
Post-GA: schedule cleanup of temporary shims and measure opt-in usage; consider making compat layer a chargeable enterprise feature.
Rollback: documented immediate flag toggle and an emergency path to redirect to native Redwood payloads if incompatibilities cause customer impact.
risks: Increased latency for compat customers due to buffering and translation.
Edge cases where streaming reassembly fails and causes incorrect function-call payloads to be delivered.
Operational cost: adapter CPU/memory overhead on busy fleets leading to capacity pressure.
False sense of parity: some OAI behaviors (undocumented client-side parsing heuristics) cannot be perfectly emulated.
Regulatory/audit impact if metadata required by customers is not faithfully preserved.
SDK fragmentation risk if server-side compatibility is partial and different SDK versions try to patch behaviors client-side.
next_steps: Finalize adapter design decision by 2025-02-17 (option A vs B).
Prototype minimal streaming delta -> token translation (PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2487).
Author compatibility test vectors and add to evaluation harness (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RESP/compatibility+vectors).
Schedule a design review with runtime, SDK, and product (invite: runtime-arch@redwood.ai) week of 2025-02-24.
Create monitoring dashboards for canary (latency, reassembly_mismatch_rate, function_call_errors).
Coordinate with solutions engineering for early customer pilots (list in comments).
Prepare migration guide draft and publish internal RFC for feedback.
Estimate infra cost delta and add to capacity plan for Q2 2025.
